mainTopic: Who counts toward a זימון (a קטן, people who ate ירק), and how much one must eat to lead ברכת המזון for others
overview: This amud finishes the long discussion about counting a קטן for a זימון. The גמרא rules like רב נחמן: a קטן who knows to Whom we bless is counted. A story about young אביי and רבא shows what that understanding looks like. Next, רב rules that nine who ate דגן and one who ate ירק join for a זימון of ten. רבי זירא learns that eight or seven also work, but he holds that six is not enough because we need a רובא דמינכר, a clearly noticeable majority. רבי ירמיה disagrees, since six is still a רוב. The גמרא then tells how שמעון בן שטח drank a cup of wine and led ברכת המזון for ינאי המלך. רבי יוחנן says this was not the standard rule: to lead others, one must eat a כזית of דגן. A ברייתא seems to say even one fig is enough. The גמרא answers that a small amount lets a person join the group, but leading it still needs a כזית of דגן. A supporting statement from רבא begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The phrase 'we are not exacting' comes to include a minor at the threshold of maturity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא's phrase 'we are not exacting with a קטן' comes to include a קטן פורח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it come to include a 'blossoming' minor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation from the previous discussion. The words 'we are not exacting with a קטן' come to include a קטן פורח, a boy right at the edge of maturity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence is phrased as a question, but here it works as the answer to what the extra words in the ברייתא add. The ברייתא includes a boy who is just reaching maturity. We do not check closely whether he has fully reached גדלות.

keyTerms.meaning: to include / to bring in (a case the text adds)
a 'blossoming' minor: a boy at the threshold of physical maturity
a minor, under the age of מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a real question waiting for an answer. In context it works as the explanation itself: the ברייתא's extra words include a קטן פורח.

phrases.english: To include a 'blossoming' (maturing) minor?
phrases.notes: Explains what the ברייתא's phrase 'we are not exacting with a minor' adds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the ברייתא from the previous part of the daf (outside this passage).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting an extra phrase in the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase 'we are not exacting' includes a קטן פורח.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב נחמן: a קטן who knows Whom we bless is counted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects all the earlier opinions and rules like רב נחמן: a קטן who understands to Whom one blesses may be counted for a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The halacha does not follow any of these teachings. Rather, it follows what רב נחמן said: a minor who knows to Whom one blesses is counted for a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final ruling on the whole debate about a קטן and זימון. It sets aside every earlier opinion and adopts רב נחמן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier opinions measured a minor by age or by physical signs. רב נחמן's test is different: it asks whether the child understands. A child who knows that the blessing goes to הקדוש ברוך הוא can be counted.

keyTerms.meaning: we count him for a זימון

steps.whatToRemember: Final halacha: a קטן who knows to Whom we bless joins the זימון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the practical rule for counting a child toward a זימון. It rests on understanding, not on physical maturity.

phrases.english: And the halacha is not in accordance with any of these teachings,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: rather, like this that Rav Nachman said:
A minor who knows to Whom one blesses —
we count him for a zimmun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole debate by setting aside all the earlier opinions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A קטן who knows to Whom one blesses is counted for a זימון.

steps.title: רבה tests young אביי and רבא on Whom we bless
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks the young אביי and רבא to Whom we bless and where He dwells. רבא points to the ceiling, and אביי goes outside and points to the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא were sitting before רבה. רבה asked them: To whom do we bless? They said: To the Merciful One. He asked: And where does the Merciful One sit? רבא pointed to the ceiling. אביי went outside and pointed toward the sky.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows what 'knowing to Whom one blesses' looks like in a child. It sets up רבה's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both children give the right answer, 'to the Merciful One.' When asked where He is, both point upward, showing they grasp that הקדוש ברוך הוא is above. רבא points to the ceiling, while אביי goes outside to point at the actual sky.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One (a name for הקדוש ברוך הוא)
the ceiling (literally 'the sky of the roofing')

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה.
phrases.english: Abaye and Rava were sitting before Rabba.
phrases.notes: They were young children at the time.

phrases.english: Rabba said to them: To whom do we bless?
They said to him: To the Merciful One.
And where does the Merciful One sit?
Rava pointed to the ceiling.
Abaye went outside,
and pointed toward the sky.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רב נחמן's standard, 'knowing to Whom one blesses.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children who understand that blessings go to הקדוש ברוך הוא, Who is above, meet the standard of 'knowing to Whom one blesses.'

steps.title: רבה predicts both will become great חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבה declares that both boys will become רבנן and quotes the saying that a cucumber is recognized from its blossom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to them: Both of you will become Sages. This is what people say: A cucumber is known from its blossom.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה reacts to the children's answers and predicts their greatness. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proverb means that greatness can be seen even at an early stage, just as you can tell a good cucumber from its flower. The children's clear understanding showed their future.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what people say (introduces a proverb)
is recognized from its blossom (early stage)

steps.whatToRemember: The story shows the kind of understanding a child needs in order to be counted for a זימון. It also shows that greatness can be recognized early.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבָּה: תַּרְוַיְיכוּ רַבָּנַן הָוֵיתוּ.
phrases.english: Rabba said to them: Both of you will become Sages.
This is what people say:
A cucumber, a cucumber is known from its blossom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of the story begun in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both children showed true understanding, and greatness shows itself early.

steps.title: Nine who ate grain and one who ate vegetables join together
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if nine ate דגן and one ate ירק, they combine to form a זימון of ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה son of רב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: If nine ate grain and one ate vegetables, they join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: can people who did not eat bread help make up a זימון of ten? רב says one person who ate only ירק can join nine who ate דגן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a זימון is built from people who ate bread or grain. רב allows one person who ate ירק to complete the ten, because nearly the whole group ate grain. The obvious next question is how many vegetable-eaters are allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the base case for the rest of the sugya, which asks how small the grain-eating majority can be.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into the ruling it introduces.

phrases.english: If nine ate grain
and one ate vegetables — they join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּשְׁעָה אָכְלוּ דָּגָן וְאֶחָד אָכַל יָרָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion about a קטן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine who ate דגן plus one who ate ירק combine for a זימון of ten.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks about eight or seven grain-eaters
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports that he asked רב יהודה whether the rule also works with eight or seven grain-eaters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I asked רב יהודה: What about eight? What about seven?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא tests how far רב's rule stretches. He asks whether eight or seven grain-eaters are still enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב spoke about nine, so it is unclear whether nine is the minimum or just one example. רבי זירא checks whether the rule still holds as more people eat only ירק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
I asked Rav Yehuda:
What about eight? What about seven?
phrases.notes: That is, eight (or seven) ate grain and the rest ate vegetables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the limits of רב's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether eight or seven grain-eaters are still enough to join with the vegetable-eaters for a זימון of ten.

steps.title: רב יהודה answers that there is no difference
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that eight and seven work the same as nine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: There is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers רבי זירא's question. Eight or seven grain-eaters also join with the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that 'nine' in רב's ruling was just an example, not a strict minimum. The ruling stretches down to at least seven.

phrases.english: He said to me: There is no difference.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Eight or seven grain-eaters also combine with the rest, just like nine.

steps.title: רבי זירא says six was obvious to him
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא adds that he did not even ask about six, because it was obvious to him that six is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: About six I certainly had no question.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains why his questions stopped at seven. He felt six grain-eaters were obviously not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six out of ten is still more than half, yet רבי זירא saw it as clearly not enough. This sets up the next step, where רבי ירמיה reads the same 'no question' in the opposite direction.

keyTerms.meaning: I had no question (it was obvious to me)

steps.confusionAlert: 'I had no question' does not tell you which way. Here רבי זירא means six is obviously NOT enough. רבי ירמיה will say it is obviously enough.

phrases.english: Six — I certainly had no question.
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is still speaking; he assumed six do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי זירא explains why he did not ask about six.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי זירא's view, six grain-eaters are obviously not enough.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה argues that six is obviously enough because it is a majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says רבי זירא was right not to ask, but for the opposite reason. If seven and eight work because they are a רוב, six is also a רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to him: You did well not to ask. There, what is the reason? Because there is a majority. Here too there is a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי זירא's assumption about six. He argues that six should obviously count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה finds the reason behind seven and eight: the grain-eaters are a רוב. Six out of ten is also a רוב, so by that same reason six should work. He agrees there was no need to ask, but only because the answer is obviously 'yes.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to him:
You did well that you did not ask,
phrases.notes: Said with a twist: the answer is obvious in the other direction.

phrases.english: there (seven, eight), what is the reason?
Because there is a majority;
here (six) too there is a majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי זירא's 'obvious' around in the opposite direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's assumption that six grain-eaters obviously do not combine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason seven and eight work is that they are a רוב. Six of ten is also a רוב, so six should obviously work.

steps.title: רבי זירא requires a noticeable majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי זירא's view: we need a רוב that is clearly noticeable, and six against four is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he (רבי זירא) held: We need a noticeable majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא against רבי ירמיה's argument. A bare majority is not enough; it has to be an obvious one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven against three is a clear majority, while six against four is too close to look like a real majority. So both רבי זירא and רבי ירמיה agree a רוב is needed. They disagree about whether a slim רוב counts.
steps.whatToRemember: Nine, eight, or seven grain-eaters can join with vegetable-eaters for a זימון of ten. For six, רבי זירא says no because there is no רובא דמינכר, and רבי ירמיה says yes because it is still a רוב.

phrases.english: But he (Rabbi Zeira) held:
We require a noticeable majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי זירא's position in the face of רבי ירמיה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the needed standard: a noticeable majority, not just any majority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any רוב is enough, so six should combine.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי זירא requires a רובא דמינכר, so six against four does not combine in his view.

steps.title: ינאי המלך has no one to lead the ברכה
steps.stepSummary: ינאי המלך and the queen eat bread, but no חכם is left to lead ברכת המזון. The queen brings her brother שמעון בן שטח after the king swears not to harm him.
steps.simpleTranslation: King ינאי and the queen ate bread together. Since he had killed the חכמים, he had no one to say the ברכה for them. He asked his wife: Who will get us a man to bless for us? She said: Swear to me that if I bring you a man, you will not hurt him. He swore, and she brought her brother, שמעון בן שטח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will connect to the rules about joining a זימון. This part sets up the scene and brings in the main character, שמעון בן שטח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ינאי had killed the חכמים, so no Torah scholar was left at his table to lead ברכת המזון. The queen protects her brother with an oath before bringing him. This sets up the question that matters later: can someone who did not eat lead the ברכה?

keyTerms.meaning: ינאי המלך, a חשמונאי king who killed the חכמים
They ate bread, literally 'wrapped up bread'
To recite the blessing, here ברכת המזון
You will not cause him harm or pain

phrases.english: King Yannai and the queen
ate bread together
and since he had killed the Sages

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ אִינִישׁ לְבָרוֹכֵי לְהוּ.
phrases.english: he had no one to recite the blessing for them.
He said to his wife:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן יָהֵיב לַן גַּבְרָא דִּמְבָרֵךְ לַן?
phrases.english: Who will give us a man who will bless for us?
She said to him: Swear to me
that if I bring you a man
you will not harm him.
He swore to her.
She brought Shimon ben Shatach, her brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: יַנַּאי מַלְכָּא וּמַלְכְּתָא כְּרִיכוּ רִיפְתָּא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing who can join a זימון, the גמרא brings a story about a man who joins a meal he did not eat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: ינאי needs someone to lead ברכת המזון, and שמעון בן שטח is brought in.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח says the Torah honors him
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח is seated between the king and queen. When the king boasts of the honor he is giving him, שמעון בן שטח answers that the Torah honors him, not the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: She sat him between the king and herself. The king said: See how much honor I give you! He answered: It is not you who honors me. The Torah honors me, as it says: 'Value her and she will raise you up. She will honor you when you embrace her.' The king said to his wife: You see, he does not accept authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a short exchange between the king and שמעון בן שטח. It is background color, not yet the halachic point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king wants credit for honoring שמעון בן שטח, but he refuses it and gives the credit to Torah. The פסוק from משלי teaches that a person who values Torah is lifted up by it. The king sees this as a refusal to bow to his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Value her (Torah) and she will raise you up (משלי ד:ח)

phrases.english: She seated him between his (seat) and hers.
He (the king) said to him: Do you see
how much honor I am giving you?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו אַתְּ קָא מוֹקְרַתְּ לִי
phrases.english: He said to him: It is not you who honors me
rather, it is the Torah that honors me,
as it is written: 'Extol her and she will exalt you;
she will bring you honor when you embrace her.'
He (the king) said to her: You see
that he does not accept authority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after שמעון בן שטח arrives at the king's table.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative point: honor comes from Torah, not from the king.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח drinks first, then leads the ברכה
steps.stepSummary: Before leading ברכת המזון, שמעון בן שטח points out that he has not eaten. He drinks a cup of wine, then takes a second cup and leads the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They gave him a cup to lead the ברכה. He said: How can I bless? Should I say, 'Blessed is He from whose food ינאי and his friends ate'? (I did not eat anything!) He drank that cup. They gave him another cup, and he led the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the halachic heart of the story. שמעון בן שטח makes himself part of the meal by drinking wine, and only then leads ברכת המזון for the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the זימון, 'שאכלנו משלו' (whose food we ate), only make sense if the leader ate too. If he had not eaten, he could only say 'ינאי and his friends ate.' So he drank the first cup to count as one who ate, and then led the ברכה on a second cup.

keyTerms.meaning: A cup of wine used for ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: שמעון בן שטח did not eat bread. He only drank wine. That is exactly why the next step questions whether what he did was really allowed.

phrases.english: They gave him a cup to recite the blessing.
He said: How shall I bless?
'Blessed is He from whose food Yannai and his companions ate'?
phrases.notes: He had eaten nothing, so he could not say 'we ate.'

phrases.english: He drank that cup,
they gave him another cup, and he blessed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the honor exchange to the actual ברכת המזון.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story seems to show that drinking a cup of wine is enough to lead others in ברכת המזון. The next step questions that.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the story, שמעון בן שטח led ברכת המזון after drinking only a cup of wine.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: leading others requires a כזית of grain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says שמעון בן שטח acted on his own and not by the standard rule. To lead others in ברכת המזון, one must eat a כזית of grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא, said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What שמעון בן שטח did, he did on his own. This is because רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A person can never help the group fulfill their obligation until he eats a כזית of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא comments on the story and says it is not a model to follow. He backs this up with a clear rule from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story could make us think a cup of wine is enough to lead the ברכה. רבי יוחנן's rule says it is not: the leader must eat a כזית of grain. So שמעון בן שטח's act was his own personal decision, not the standard הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He did it on his own, not according to the standard rule
Fulfills the obligation for the group

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba, said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
What Shimon ben Shatach did,
he did on his own,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for so said Rabbi Chiya bar Abba in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן
phrases.english: One can never fulfill the obligation of the many
until he eats an olive-bulk of grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח דַּעֲבַד לְגַרְמֵיהּ הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the story so it does not set a הלכה, based on רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the person leading ברכת המזון for others must have eaten a כזית of grain. A cup of wine alone is not enough.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To lead others in ברכת המזון, one must eat a כזית of grain. שמעון בן שטח's act was not the standard rule.

steps.title: Challenge: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says even one fig is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with a ברייתא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that someone who dipped in brine or ate just one dried fig with the group joins them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this from a ברייתא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If someone came in and reclined with them, even if he only dipped with them in brine, and only ate one dried fig with them, he joins them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule with an earlier source that seems to say the opposite. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן requires a כזית of grain to lead others. But רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says even a tiny amount of non-grain food, like one fig, is enough to join. If joining is that easy, why did רבי יוחנן say שמעון בן שטח acted on his own?

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, an objection from a תנאי source
Reclined, sat down to the meal
Brine, salty fish liquid for dipping

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the word מצטרף, 'joins.' The challenge assumes that joining the group also means being able to lead it. The next step answers by separating these two ideas.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If one came in and reclined with them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לֹא טִבֵּל עִמָּהֶם אֶלָּא בְּצִיר,
phrases.english: even if he only dipped with them in brine,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אָכַל עִמָּהֶם אֶלָּא גְּרוֹגֶרֶת אַחַת —
phrases.english: and ate with them only a single dried fig,
he joins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that one must eat a כזית of grain to lead others in ברכת המזון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says even a single fig or a dip in brine is enough to join the group. That suggests grain, and even a כזית, are not required. So שמעון בן שטח's cup of wine should have been fine.

steps.title: Joining the group is different from leading the ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא only says a small amount of food lets a person join the group. To lead others in ברכת המזון, he still needs a כזית of דגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does join them. But to fulfill the obligation of the many on their behalf, he must first eat an olive-size amount of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. It says the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן are talking about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only deals with צירוף, being counted as part of the group. רבי יוחנן was talking about something bigger: being the one who says the ברכה for everyone. A small amount of food is enough for the first, but the second needs a כזית of דגן, so the ברייתא does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: He certainly joins in. The doubled verb stresses agreement with the ברייתא on this point.
To fulfill their obligation for them, by saying the ברכה on their behalf
The many, meaning the rest of the group
Grain, the food that gives the strongest obligation of ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that being counted in the group and leading the group are the same thing. Someone can be counted toward the זימון without being allowed to say the ברכה on everyone's behalf.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a two-level rule for ברכת המזון. A smaller amount of food is enough to join the group, but a full כזית of דגן is needed to lead it.

phrases.english: He indeed joins them
phrases.notes: The גמרא agrees with what the ברייתא actually says.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן —
phrases.english: but to fulfill the obligation of the many
phrases.notes: This is a different level, leading the ברכה for others.

phrases.english: not until he eats an olive-size amount of grain.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's rule, now shown to stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרוֹפֵי מִצְטָרֵף אֲבָל לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 by limiting the ברייתא to joining the group.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two levels of law: joining (צירוף) versus leading others (להוציא את הרבים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that a person who ate only a fig counts fully, which would also let him lead the ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only allows him to join. Leading still needs a כזית of דגן, as רבי יוחנן said.

steps.title: A supporting statement from רבא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a statement of רב חנא בר יהודה in the name of רבא that agrees with this rule. It opens with 'even if he did not', and the rest continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב חנא בר יהודה said in the name of רבא: Even if he did not...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a support for the rule it just gave. Here we only see the opening of רבא's statement, and it finishes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words איתמר נמי mean that another אמורא said the same idea independently, which strengthens the answer in step 16. The word אפילו tells us רבא will name a minimal amount of eating. His statement finishes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated. This brings an אמורא's statement that backs up what was just said.
Even. It shows the case is pushed to the smallest amount.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥana bar Yehuda said in the name of Rava:
phrases.notes: The attribution is merged into this step.

phrases.english: Even if he did not...
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an independent statement from an אמורא that backs up the distinction made in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between joining the group with a small amount of food and leading the ברכה with a כזית of דגן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of רב חנא בר יהודה in the name of רבא, which continues on the next amud.
